content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"All four blind responses converge on the same core: marriage/bride imagery symbolizes the covenant union between Christ (bridegroom) and the Church or people of God (bride), built on the Old Testament portrayal of Israel as YHWH's wife, culminating in the eschatological marriage supper of the Lamb. Key texts cited across responses are Ephesians 5:22-33, Revelation 19:7-9 and 21:2-9, Hosea 1-3, Isaiah 54, Ezekiel 16, and Genesis 2:24 read with Ephesians 5. Alternatives (New Jerusalem, individual soul, dispensational Israel/Church distinction) are treated as refinements of who exactly the bride is, not rejections of the covenant-marriage core.","book_summary":"The book defines marriage/bride as 'the covenant union of God and His people — the one-flesh bond God joins: the wife called by the Husband's name, brought under His wing,' citing Genesis 2:24, Ezekiel 16:8 (God covenanting with Israel under His skirt/wing), Ephesians 5:31-32 (one flesh; Christ and the church), and Revelation 19:7 (the marriage of the Lamb).","consensus_core_identification":"Covenant marital union between God/Christ (husband/bridegroom) and His people (Israel in the OT, the Church in the NT) as the bride/wife.","book_core_identification":"Covenant union of God and His people — a divinely joined one-flesh bond in which the people are the wife taken under the Husband's covenant protection and name.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None material. The book states the referent broadly as 'God and His people,' which unifies the Israel-as-YHWH's-wife strand (Ezek 16:8) and the Christ-Church strand (Eph 5:31-32; Rev 19:7). This unified formulation is explicitly anticipated in the consensus (Response C's 'broad, unified sense encompassing both Israel and the Church' alternative, and all responses' treatment of OT imagery as the foundation of the NT usage), so it does not constitute a boundary shift.","material_contradiction":"None. Nothing in the book entry denies or replaces the Christ-Church identification; Ephesians 5:32 and Revelation 19:7 are printed with the entry, showing the Christ-Church application is retained within the broader God-and-His-people framing.","rationale":"Reduced to minimum cores, both readings identify marriage/bride as the covenant marital union between God/Christ and His people. The book's phrasing ('one-flesh bond God joins,' 'under His wing') adds imagery from Genesis 2:24 and Ezekiel 16:8 but does not alter the referent, extension, or conditions. Its ecumenical framing spanning Israel and the Church tracks the consensus's own account, in which OT Israel imagery grounds the NT Christ-Church usage. Differences are wording and emphasis, not identification, so MATCH with EQUIVALENT core and SAME_CASES extension.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book's referent 'God and His people' subtly broadens beyond the consensus's headline 'Christ and the Church,' making it REFINED (BOOK_BROADENS). But this unified reading is itself listed within the consensus responses (explicitly as an alternative in Response C and implicitly in all responses' OT-foundation framing), and the entry's own citations (Eph 5:32; Rev 19:7) include the Christ-Church sense, so the broadening claim collapses into wording rather than a material extension change.","confidence":"high"}
